'''''Gastroclonium reflexum''''' is a small red marine seaweed.

==Description==
''Gastroclonium ovatum'' is a small [[alga]] which grows to 15 cm long. The branches are cylindrical, grow from a branched [[holdfast (biology)|holdfast]] and branch irregularly. It shows short branches which are hollow with bladder-like or vesicle-like branches - rather elongate with a single joint. In colour it is dark purplish red.<ref name = "Bunker">Bunker, F.StP.D., Brodie, J.A., Maggs, C.A. and Bunker, A.R. 2017 ''Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland Second Edition'' Wild Nature Press, Plymouth, UK {{ISBN|978-0-9955673-3-7}}</ref><ref name="Irvine">Irvine, L.M.1983. ''Seaweeds of the British Isles Volume 1 Rhodophyta Part 2A Cryptomeniales (Sensu stricto) Palmariales, Rhodymeniales'' British Museum (Natural History) {{ISBN|0-565-00871-4}}</ref><ref>Dickinson, C.I. 1963, ''British Seaweeds'' The Kew Series</ref>

==Habitat==
Found in rock pools in the littoral or upper sublittoral, epilithic or epiphytic.<ref name="Irvine"/>

==Distribution==
Recorded from the [[British Isles]], [[Mauritania]], [[Canary Islands]]<ref name="Irvine"/> and the [[Channel Islands]].<ref name="Bunker"/>

==Reproduction==
The sexes are separate. The female [[cystocarp]]s occur on the branches and the tetrasporangia in the cortex of the vesicles.<ref name="Bunker"/>

==Similar species==
''Gastroclonium reflexum'' distinguished by many branches being reflexed<ref name="Irvine"/> and ''Chylocladia verticillata''.<ref name="Bunker"/>
